replication.target_description: Primary replication of Kidd and Castano experiment 5, literary versus popular fiction. The broad affective theory-of-mind description and p. 7 locator do not uniquely distinguish RMET from the Yoni outcomes; p. 7 of this article (printed p. 16) reports both.

notes: Identity verified from canonical text: title Leidt het Lezen van Literaire Fictie tot Meer Empathie?, subtitle Een Replicatiestudie; author header names Katinka Dijkstra, Peter Verkoeijen, Iris van Kuijk, Soke Yee Chow, Annelies Bakker and Rolf Zwaan; De Psycholoog, October 2015, printed pp. 10–21. Full primary replication report with methods, results, discussion and Appendix 2, matching the supplied reference and source URL; no replication DOI asserted. No PDF path supplied. Only the three assigned unfinished fields were examined for completion; other core fields are placeholders. Target ambiguity: the neutral description encompasses RMET and affective Yoni tests, while the locator identifies a page with both, without a unique outcome/test. Candidate RMET condition effect is printed as partial correlation .071 (pp. 16, 21); no numeric condition-effect p is printed, only a nonsignificant verdict and adjusted-mean confidence intervals. Appendix 2 p=.416 is the entire five-predictor regression model test F(5,288)=1.004, not the RMET condition coefficient; it must not be paired with .071. Candidate Yoni text-type main effect is F < 1, p=.329, partial eta-squared=.003 (pp. 16, 21), aggregating cognitive/affective types and difficulty levels, rather than a separately identified affective-only contrast. Table 3 on printed p. 17 contains multiple outcome means/SDs by story/condition, not a unique target effect. No Cohen d for the replication target is printed in these results; Table 1 Cohen d values describe original experiments and cannot substitute. Retain candidates without selecting one or converting metrics. Appendix 2 documents RMET model n=294, but this is only a candidate model N, not an assigned extraction or globally matched target. No N calculation was performed. Author verdict applies to the replication generally and is explicit despite unresolved outcome correspondence.
